document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: The insulation line should run unbroken through this junction.
rules.why: Where the insulation stops or has a gap, heat leaks out and the cold spot can gather condensation and mould.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: The damp-proof course should be at least 150 mm above the adjoining ground level.
rules.why: Rain splashes up from the ground and soil gets banked against walls; keeping the damp-proof course well above it stops water rising into the wall.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: The floor's damp-proof membrane should link to the wall's damp-proof course.
rules.why: If there is a gap between the floor membrane and the wall's damp-proof course, ground moisture can find its way round the join.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: A cavity tray should be shown over the opening.
rules.why: Water that gets into the cavity runs down the inside of the outer wall; over an opening it needs a tray to lead it back outside instead of onto the frame.

document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: Where the ventilation strategy relies on background ventilators, the window should show one.
rules.why: Homes need a steady supply of fresh air to clear moisture and pollutants; whether a vent is needed here depends on the ventilation system chosen.

document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: The cavity should be closed around the opening.
rules.why: An open cavity at the edge of an opening lets fire and smoke travel through the wall unseen, so the cavity is closed around openings.

document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: The detail should show a cavity closer.
rules.why: Closing the cavity at openings stops fire and smoke spreading through the hidden space inside the wall.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: A damp-proof course should be shown under the sill.
rules.why: Sills collect rain and their joints can leak; a damp-proof layer beneath stops that water soaking down into the wall.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: The sill should project beyond the face of the wall.
rules.why: A sill that sticks out, ideally with a drip underneath, throws rainwater clear of the wall instead of letting it run down the face.

document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: At a principal entrance, the threshold upstand should total no more than 15 mm.
rules.why: A higher step at the front door is a trip hazard and a barrier to wheelchairs, buggies and anyone unsteady on their feet.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: A damp-proof course should be shown below the threshold.
rules.why: Door thresholds sit close to the ground where water collects, so the wall below needs a damp-proof layer linked to the floor.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: Where the roof space is ventilated, the eaves should show a clear ventilation path.
rules.why: Warm moist air from the house can condense in a cold roof space; air moving through at the eaves carries that moisture away.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: The verge should be mechanically fixed, for example with a dry verge system, not held by mortar alone.
rules.why: Wind pulls hardest at the edges of a roof; tiles held only by mortar can loosen and blow off.

rules.message: The membrane upstand should be at least 150 mm above the finished roof surface.
rules.why: Water can pond or be blown against the parapet; the waterproof layer has to turn up high enough that it cannot get over the top into the wall.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: A damp-proof course should be shown under the coping.
rules.why: Coping joints are not watertight for ever; a damp-proof layer underneath stops water that gets through from soaking down the wall.

rules.message: The membrane upstand should be at least 150 mm above the finished roof surface.
rules.why: Where a flat roof meets a wall, water pools against it; the waterproof layer must turn up the wall high enough to stay above it.

rules.message: A cover flashing should overlap the top of the upstand.
rules.why: The top edge of the upstand is a weak point; a flashing over it stops rain running down the wall and in behind the membrane.

document.edition: Edition to be confirmed by the signer

rules.message: A cavity tray should be shown in the wall above the roof.
rules.why: Water in the cavity above a lower roof would otherwise run down behind the roof finish; a tray leads it out above the flashing.

document.edition: Volume 1: Dwellings (edition to be confirmed by the signer)

rules.message: Where the balcony structure passes through the wall, a thermal break should be shown.
rules.why: A balcony slab running straight through the wall carries heat out like a radiator fin, making a cold patch inside that can grow mould.

typical_details.title: Window head in a cavity wall
principles: A lintel carries both leaves over the opening.
A cavity tray with stop ends sheds water from the cavity outwards.
The frame sits in line with the cavity insulation so the insulation line is unbroken.

typical_details.title: Window jamb in a cavity wall
principles: The cavity is closed at the reveal with an insulated cavity closer.
The frame overlaps the closer so there is no gap in the insulation line.

typical_details.title: Window sill in a cavity wall
principles: The sill projects beyond the wall face and has a drip.
A damp-proof course under the sill is turned up at the back.

typical_details.title: Door threshold at ground floor
principles: A damp-proof course below the threshold links to the floor's damp-proof membrane.
At a principal entrance the threshold upstand is kept low for level access.

typical_details.title: Eaves of a pitched tiled roof
principles: Loft insulation meets the wall insulation so the insulation line is unbroken.
A ventilation path at the eaves keeps a cold roof space dry.
The fascia and gutter collect water clear of the wall.

typical_details.title: Verge at a gable
principles: Verge tiles are mechanically fixed, for example with a dry verge system.
The verge overhangs the gable to throw water clear of the wall.

typical_details.title: Parapet at a warm flat roof
principles: Insulation sits above the deck; the membrane sits above the insulation.
The membrane turns up the parapet as an upstand.
A coping with a drip caps the wall, with a damp-proof course beneath it.

typical_details.title: Warm flat roof abutting a wall
principles: The membrane turns up the wall as an upstand.
A cover flashing overlaps the top of the upstand.
A cavity tray in the wall above leads cavity water out over the flashing.

typical_details.title: Ground floor to wall junction with DPC
principles: The damp-proof course sits well above the outside ground.
The floor's damp-proof membrane links to the damp-proof course.
Floor and wall insulation meet so the insulation line is unbroken.

typical_details.title: Cavity closer at an opening
principles: An insulated cavity closer closes the cavity at the reveal.
The closer keeps the insulation line continuous to the frame.

typical_details.title: Cavity wall to foundation
principles: The foundation is designed by the engineer for the ground conditions.
The cavity below ground is filled so the leaves are supported and water cannot collect.

typical_details.title: Balcony threshold
principles: A thermal break separates the balcony structure from the floor inside.
The balcony surface falls away from the door.
The membrane turns up at the threshold under the door frame.

typical_details.title: Steel beam bearing on an inner leaf
principles: The beam, padstone and bearing length come from the engineer.
The beam bears on the inner leaf, never bridging the cavity.

coverage.statement: GB-ENG Residential v0.1.0 (Tier 1) runs 19 automated checks covering moisture, thermal, ventilation, condensation, cavity barriers, access, weathertightness. All are unverified and unsigned, so every result is a flag for professional review, never a pass. Checks not available: structural, fire stopping, acoustic, drainage.
